title: Bethlehem and Zion compared
english: If our Savior had not humbled himself and become obedient to the point of death (Philippians 2:8), servants would never have been called kinsmen, nor would the clay ever have been called the father of the potter.
In Zion I greet Bethlehem as though she were present; in the daughter I see the mother.

In you one torch-bearing star was kindled, but in her many were kindled. That star guided the Magi, but she gave torchlight to Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people from all the nations with light like lightning.
You draw milk from virgin breasts, but she draws down the Spirit from the Father's bosom.
translator_notes: The Greek text is fragmentary, ending abruptly after 'ἀλλ\' ἡ Σιὼν' with no further words supplied; the translation renders the extant text literally with trailing ellipsis to indicate the break.
The phrase 'τῷ φωτὶ τῆς ἀστραπῆς' is translated as 'to the light of the lightning' to reflect the literal meaning of 'astrape' as lightning, not torch.

The clauses 'Σὺ γάλα ἕλκεις ἐκ μασθῶν παρθενικῶν' and 'αὕτη πνεῦμα ἐκ κόλπων καταγει πατρικῶν' are translated directly as 'You draw milk from virgin breasts' and 'this one brings down the spirit from paternal bosoms' to preserve the original agency and meaning.
No direct biblical quotations are present in the extant Greek fragment; thus no inline scripture references are added.
The phrase 'Ἐν σοὶ δᾳδοῦχος ἀστὴρ εἷς ἀνήφθη' corresponds to 'In you a foster-father one star has risen' and is now fully integrated into the sentence.
The verb 'ἐδᾳδούχησε' is rendered as 'has guided' and is now properly included in the clause regarding the nations.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia i in sanctum Lazarum (Khazarzar) u01 open
orientation: Hesychius, priest of Jerusalem, opens his homily on James the brother of the Lord and David the ancestor of God by contrasting Bethlehem, where Christ was born, with Zion, where the Church now receives him.
